description: Checks primary and O-level mathematics content knowledge and the teaching methods used to address common pupil misconceptions.

competencies.name: Number and Numeracy
competencies.description: Fractions, decimals, place value and operations with numbers.

competencies.name: Algebra
competencies.description: Solving equations, expanding and simplifying expressions.

competencies.name: Geometry and Measurement
competencies.description: Area, perimeter, units and right-angled triangles.

competencies.name: Statistics and Probability
competencies.description: Mean, data handling and simple probability.

competencies.name: Pedagogy and Misconceptions
competencies.description: Teaching for understanding, diagnosing errors and responding to results.

questions.text: What is 3/4 ÷ 1/2?
questions.explanation: Dividing by 1/2 means multiplying by 2: 3/4 × 2 = 6/4 = 1 1/2.

questions.text: A Standard Six pupil says 0.35 is bigger than 0.5 "because 35 is bigger than 5". What is the best way to correct this?

options.text: Write both as 0.35 and 0.50 on a place-value chart and compare tenths first
Give the pupil ten more decimal sums to practise without discussion
Mark it wrong and move on because the rule is in the textbook
Tell the pupil that the number with more digits is always smaller

questions.explanation: The pupil treats the digits after the point as a whole number. A place-value chart with equal decimal places shows 5 tenths is greater than 3 tenths.

questions.text: Solve for x: 3x − 7 = 11.
questions.explanation: Add 7 to both sides to get 3x = 18, then divide by 3 to get x = 6.

questions.text: Expand (x + 3)².

options.text: x² + 3x + 9
x² + 6x + 9
x² + 9

questions.explanation: (x + 3)(x + 3) = x² + 3x + 3x + 9 = x² + 6x + 9. The middle term is the common error when pupils write x² + 9.

questions.text: Which of these expressions are equal to 2(x − 3) + 4 for every value of x? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation: 2(x − 3) + 4 = 2x − 6 + 4 = 2x − 2, which also equals 2(x − 1).

questions.text: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 6 cm. What is its area?

options.text: 30 cm²
60 cm²
32 cm²
100 cm²

questions.explanation: Area of a triangle = 1/2 × base × height = 1/2 × 10 × 6 = 30 cm².

questions.text: A rectangular classroom floor is 5 m by 12 m. What is the length of the diagonal?
questions.explanation: The diagonal is the hypotenuse: √(5² + 12²) = √169 = 13 m.

questions.text: A pupil writes "area of a 4 m by 3 m rectangle = 12 m, perimeter = 14 m²". How would you best help the pupil?

options.text: Use square tiles to show that area counts squares (m²) while perimeter is the length around the edge (m)
Ask the pupil to memorise the rule "area uses squares" and write it out ten times in the exercise book
Tell the pupil to simply swap the two units around because the textbook example shows them that way
Accept the answer and move on since the numbers 12 and 14 are correct even if the units are not

questions.explanation: A concrete model links the unit to what is being measured. Correct numbers with wrong units show a conceptual gap that should be fixed.

questions.text: The mean of five numbers is 8. A sixth number, 14, is added. What is the new mean?
questions.explanation: The original total is 5 × 8 = 40. The new total is 54, and 54 ÷ 6 = 9.

questions.text: A bag has 3 red, 5 blue and 2 green balls. One ball is picked at random. What is the probability that it is NOT blue?
questions.explanation: There are 10 balls and 5 are not blue, so the probability is 5/10 = 1/2.

questions.text: Your pupils solve equations by chanting "change side, change sign" but cannot explain why. What is the best next step?

options.text: Let pupils who get answers right skip the explanation and move on to harder problems
Give more examples so the chant becomes automatic and pupils answer faster each time
Replace the chant with a longer list of rules to memorise for each type of equation
Use a balance picture so pupils see the same operation done on both sides

questions.explanation: Understanding the balance idea (doing the same to both sides) prevents rule-based errors when equations change form.

questions.text: About 60% of your class got the fractions question wrong in a monthly test. Which actions are most useful? Select all that apply.

options.text: Look through the scripts to find the most common error patterns
Move on to the next topic because the syllabus time is short
Reteach with concrete or drawn models, then check understanding with a short quiz
Repeat the same lesson in the same way at a louder pace
Give targeted practice on the weak steps and return marked work with feedback

questions.explanation: Diagnosing errors, reteaching in a different way and giving feedback address the cause of the poor results; moving on or repeating unchanged does not.

description: Checks English grammar knowledge and the ability to teach reading, writing, speaking and listening to second-language learners.

competencies.name: Grammar and Language Knowledge
competencies.description: Accurate knowledge of grammar, tenses, word forms and pronunciation.

competencies.name: Reading and Comprehension
competencies.description: Teaching reading skills and developing understanding of texts.

competencies.name: Writing
competencies.description: Teaching the writing process and giving useful feedback.

competencies.name: Listening and Speaking
competencies.description: Developing oral skills and pronunciation in the classroom.

competencies.name: Second-Language Learners and Assessment
competencies.description: Supporting learners whose first language is Kiswahili or a mother tongue, and assessing fairly.

questions.text: Choose the correct word: "She ___ to school every day."

options.text: going
goes
go
gone

questions.explanation: With a third-person singular subject in the simple present, the verb takes -s/-es: she goes.

questions.text: Which sentence is correct?

options.text: I am living in Dodoma since the year 2015.
I lived in Dodoma since 2015.
I have lived in Dodoma since 2015.
I have lived in Dodoma for 2015.

questions.explanation: "Since" is used with the starting point of a period and the present perfect, not the simple past or continuous.

questions.text: Which sentence contains a dangling modifier?

options.text: Amina was walking to school when the rain began.
Walking to school, the rain began to fall heavily.
While we walked to school, the rain began to fall.
Walking to school, Amina got wet in the rain.

questions.explanation: The opening phrase "walking to school" should describe a person, but the subject that follows is "the rain", so the modifier dangles.

questions.text: A pupil needs to find the date of an event in a long passage as quickly as possible. Which reading skill is most useful?

options.text: Scanning
Summarising
Intensive reading
Reading aloud

questions.explanation: Scanning means looking quickly for specific information such as a date or a name.

questions.text: Your pupils read a passage aloud fluently but cannot answer questions about it. What should you do?

options.text: Ask them to memorise the whole passage so they can answer the questions from memory the next day
Let them read the passage aloud many more times until they can remember most of the details
Teach strategies such as predicting, pre-teaching key words and asking questions as they read
Stop asking comprehension questions because fluent reading already shows that they understand

questions.explanation: Fluency and comprehension are different skills. Explicit strategies help pupils understand what they decode.

questions.text: Which activities are useful BEFORE pupils read a text? Select all that apply.

options.text: Giving a spelling test on every word in the text
Asking pupils to write a final summary of the text
Discussing what pupils already know about the topic
Teaching a few key words that pupils need to understand the text
Predicting what the text is about from the title and pictures

questions.explanation: Pre-reading activities activate prior knowledge and prepare vocabulary. A summary can only be written after reading.

questions.text: Which is the usual order of the stages in the writing process?

options.text: Plan, edit, draft, publish, revise
Draft, plan, edit, revise, publish
Plan, draft, revise, edit, publish
Draft, edit, plan, revise, publish

questions.explanation: Writers plan first, draft, revise ideas and organisation, then edit spelling and grammar, and finally publish or share.

questions.text: Pupils' compositions contain many spelling, tense and punctuation errors. Which feedback approach is best?

options.text: Rewrite every sentence correctly for the pupil so the final copy has no errors at all
Focus on one or two recurring error types per piece and let pupils fix them
Give only a mark and no comments so that pupils work out their mistakes themselves
Ignore the errors completely so pupils do not lose confidence in their writing

questions.explanation: Selective feedback is manageable for learners and helps them notice and fix patterns themselves.

questions.text: Several shy pupils never speak English in class. What is the best strategy?

options.text: Let only the confident pupils answer so that lessons move faster and no time is wasted
Start with pair or small-group speaking tasks before asking for answers in front of everyone
Call on them first so they get used to speaking in front of everyone in the class
Give lower marks to pupils who stay silent so that they are forced to speak up in lessons

questions.explanation: Low-pressure pair and group work builds confidence and gives every pupil more speaking practice.

questions.text: In standard English, how is the word "record" stressed when it is a noun (a school record) and when it is a verb (to record a song)?

options.text: Both: reCORD
Noun: REcord, verb: reCORD
Both: REcord
Noun: reCORD, verb: REcord

questions.explanation: In many English noun–verb pairs, the noun is stressed on the first syllable and the verb on the second.

questions.text: During an English lesson a pupil gives a correct idea in Kiswahili because she lacks the English words. What is the best response?

options.text: Tell her that Kiswahili is forbidden in class and ignore her answer completely
Translate the whole lesson into Kiswahili from now on so that nobody has difficulty
Move on to another pupil without comment and hope that someone else gives the idea in English
Accept the idea, give her the English phrase and ask her to repeat it in a sentence

questions.explanation: Using the learner's first language briefly as a bridge supports understanding while still moving her towards English.

questions.text: You want to assess your pupils' speaking fairly. Which practices are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Test speaking only with a written grammar exam
Observe pupils during pair work using a checklist and note examples
Use a simple rubric with clear criteria that pupils know in advance
Give higher marks to pupils who sound most like a native speaker
Give feedback on both fluency and accuracy

questions.explanation: Speaking should be assessed through speaking, using shared criteria. Intelligibility matters more than accent.

description: Checks Kiswahili grammar, comprehension, composition and literature knowledge together with the methods used to teach and assess them.

competencies.name: Sarufi na Matumizi ya Lugha
competencies.description: Sarufi: ngeli, nyakati, ukanushaji na aina za maneno.

competencies.name: Ufahamu na Msamiati
competencies.description: Kufundisha ufahamu wa kifungu na maana za maneno.

competencies.name: Insha na Uandishi
competencies.description: Kufundisha uandishi wa insha na barua.

competencies.name: Fasihi
competencies.description: Fasihi simulizi na andishi, methali, maudhui na dhamira.

competencies.name: Mbinu za Ufundishaji na Tathmini
competencies.description: Mbinu bora za kufundisha na kupima stadi za lugha.

questions.text: Chagua wingi sahihi wa sentensi "Mtoto analia."

options.text: Vitoto wanalia.
Watoto analia.
Watoto wanalia.
Mtoto wanalia.

questions.explanation: Wingi wa "mtoto" ni "watoto" na kiambishi cha kitenzi hubadilika kuwa "wa-": wanalia.

questions.text: Chagua ukanushaji sahihi wa sentensi "Nilikula chakula."

options.text: Sitakula chakula.
Sinakula chakula.
Sikula chakula.
Sijala chakula.

questions.explanation: Wakati uliopita unakanushwa kwa "ku" baada ya kiambishi cha nafsi: sikula. "Sijala" ni ukanushaji wa wakati timilifu.

questions.text: Katika sentensi "Mwalimu mrefu amenunua vitabu vitatu vizuri", ni maneno yapi ni vivumishi? (Chagua zote zinazofaa — select all that apply.)

options.text: Mwalimu
mrefu
vitatu
vizuri
amenunua

questions.explanation: Vivumishi huelezea nomino: "mrefu" (sifa), "vitatu" (idadi) na "vizuri" (sifa). "Amenunua" ni kitenzi na "Mwalimu" ni nomino.

questions.text: Chagua sentensi yenye upatanisho wa kisarufi sahihi.

options.text: Miti mirefu zimeanguka.
Miti mirefu imeanguka.
Miti mrefu imeanguka.
Miti mirefu yameanguka.

questions.explanation: "Miti" ni wingi wa "mti" (ngeli ya U-I), kwa hivyo kivumishi ni "mirefu" na kiambishi cha kitenzi ni "i-": imeanguka.

questions.text: Nini maana ya methali "Haraka haraka haina baraka"?

options.text: Haraka ni dalili ya mtu mwenye bahati na mafanikio makubwa
Kufanya mambo kwa pupa mara nyingi huleta makosa au hasara
Mtu anayefanya kazi haraka hupata baraka nyingi kuliko wengine
Kazi iliyofanywa kwa haraka hulipwa zaidi kuliko kazi ya polepole

questions.explanation: Methali hii inaonya kuwa kukimbilia jambo bila kujipa muda wa kutosha huleta makosa.

questions.text: Ni mfano upi wa tathmini endelevu (ya kujenga) darasani?

options.text: Kuuliza maswali mafupi wakati wa somo na kutoa mrejesho mara moja
Kutoa alama bila kurudisha kazi kwa wanafunzi
Kutangaza nafasi ya darasani mwishoni mwa mwaka pekee
Kufanya mtihani mmoja tu wa mwisho wa mwaka

questions.explanation: Tathmini endelevu hufanyika wakati wa kujifunza na humsaidia mwalimu kurekebisha ufundishaji mara moja.

questions.text: Mwanafunzi anasema "dhamira ya riwaya ni muhtasari wa hadithi yote". Mwalimu afanye nini?

options.text: Amwambie mwanafunzi akariri maana ya dhamira bila mfano wowote kutoka kitabuni
Aeleze kuwa dhamira ni wazo kuu au ujumbe wa mwandishi, kisha atoe mfano mmoja
Akubali jibu kwa sababu muhtasari wa hadithi na dhamira ni kitu kimoja kabisa
Aache kufundisha dhamira kwa sababu ni ngumu kwa wanafunzi wa darasa hili

questions.explanation: Dhamira ni ujumbe mkuu mwandishi anaotaka kuwasilisha, tofauti na muhtasari wa matukio. Mfano halisi husaidia kuelewa.

questions.text: Wanafunzi wanasoma kifungu vizuri kwa sauti lakini hawawezi kujibu maswali ya ufahamu. Mwalimu afanye nini?

options.text: Awaambie wasome kifungu kwa sauti mara nyingi zaidi hadi wakikumbuke maneno yote ndani yake
Ajibu maswali yote mwenyewe ubaoni ili wanafunzi wanakili majibu kwenye daftari lao
Awafundishe mbinu za kusoma kwa kuelewa: kutabiri, kuuliza maswali na kufupisha kifungu
Awaambie wakariri kifungu chote na kukisema neno kwa neno mbele ya darasa zima

questions.explanation: Kusoma kwa ufasaha si sawa na kuelewa. Mbinu za wazi za ufahamu humsaidia mwanafunzi kutafuta maana.

questions.text: Chagua kinyume cha neno "ukarimu".

options.text: ubahili
uvivu
ushujaa
unyenyekevu

questions.explanation: "Ukarimu" ni kutoa kwa moyo mkunjufu; kinyume chake ni "ubahili", yaani kukataa kutoa.

questions.text: Ni kauli ipi inaeleza tofauti sahihi kati ya barua rasmi na barua ya kirafiki?

options.text: Barua rasmi haina tarehe wala anwani ya mwandishi, lakini barua ya kirafiki inazo zote mbili
Barua ya kirafiki lazima iwe na kichwa cha barua na anwani mbili za pande zote
Barua rasmi huandikwa kwa lugha ya mitaani ili ieleweke kwa urahisi na kila msomaji
Barua rasmi ina kichwa cha barua na lugha ya heshima; ya kirafiki hutumia lugha ya kawaida

questions.explanation: Barua rasmi hufuata muundo maalum na lugha ya heshima, huku barua ya kirafiki ikiwa huru zaidi.

questions.text: Insha za wanafunzi wako zina mawazo mazuri lakini hazina mpangilio wa aya. Ni hatua ipi ni bora?

options.text: Kufundisha muundo wa aya (wazo kuu na maelezo) na kuwafanya wapange mpango mfupi
Kuwaambia waandike insha ndefu zaidi bila mpango ili wapate mawazo mengi zaidi
Kutoa alama tu bila maoni yoyote na kuendelea na mada inayofuata mara moja
Kurekebisha insha zote mwenyewe na kuziandika upya kabla ya kuzirudisha

questions.explanation: Mpango mfupi na muundo wa aya husaidia wanafunzi kupanga mawazo kabla ya kuandika.

questions.text: Unataka kupima stadi ya kuzungumza ya wanafunzi. Ni njia zipi zinafaa? (Chagua zote zinazofaa — select all that apply.)

options.text: Kutoa mrejesho kuhusu ufasaha na usahihi wa lugha
Kutumia kigezo wazi (rubriki) wanachokijua mapema
Kutoa alama za juu kwa wanaozungumza kwa sauti kubwa zaidi
Kuwaangalia wanafunzi wakati wa majadiliano ya vikundi na kuandika vielelezo
Kutumia mtihani wa kuandika sarufi pekee

questions.explanation: Stadi ya kuzungumza hupimwa kwa kuzungumza, kwa vigezo vilivyo wazi na mrejesho. Sauti kubwa si kipimo cha ubora wa lugha.

description: Checks primary and O-level science content knowledge, safe practical work and ways of correcting common misconceptions.

competencies.name: Physics Concepts
competencies.description: Forces, motion and light at primary and O-level.

competencies.name: Chemistry Concepts
competencies.description: Matter, acids and bases, chemical change and reaction rates.

competencies.name: Biology Concepts
competencies.description: Cells, health, genetics and human body systems.

competencies.name: Practical Work and Lab Safety
competencies.description: Safe handling of materials, fair tests and scientific method.

competencies.name: Teaching Science and Misconceptions
competencies.description: Explaining concepts, correcting misconceptions and teaching with limited resources.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of force?

options.text: Newton
Joule
Watt
Pascal

questions.explanation: Force is measured in newtons (N). Joules measure energy, watts measure power and pascals measure pressure.

questions.text: A bus travels 150 km in 2.5 hours. What is its average speed?

options.text: 60 km/h
75 km/h
375 km/h
6 km/h

questions.explanation: Average speed = distance ÷ time = 150 ÷ 2.5 = 60 km/h.

questions.text: A pupil insists that a heavy stone always falls faster than a light one. What is the best way to address this?

options.text: Tell the pupil the answer is wrong and move on to the next topic without any demonstration
Agree, because heavier objects feel a stronger pull of gravity and so must always fall faster to the ground than light ones
Ask the pupil to copy the definition of gravity into the notebook and learn it by heart for the next test on Friday
Let pupils test it: drop two objects of different mass together, then a flat and a crumpled paper

questions.explanation: In air, shape affects air resistance, but without it all objects fall with the same acceleration. A simple test helps pupils confront the idea.

questions.text: Pure water at room temperature has a pH of about:
questions.explanation: A neutral solution such as pure water has a pH of about 7; acids are below 7 and alkalis above 7.

questions.text: Which of these are chemical changes? Select all that apply.

options.text: Wood burning
Iron rusting
Ice melting
Sugar dissolving in water
Cooking an egg

questions.explanation: Chemical changes form new substances. Melting and dissolving are physical changes that can be reversed more easily.

questions.text: According to collision theory, why does a reaction go faster when the temperature is raised?

options.text: The particles become smaller when heated and so they react with each other more easily
The activation energy of the reaction becomes smaller because the mixture is hotter
More particles are created when the mixture is heated, so there are more to react
Particles move faster, collide more often and more collisions have enough energy

questions.explanation: Heating increases particle speed and energy, so there are more frequent and more successful collisions.

questions.text: In which part of a plant cell does photosynthesis take place?

options.text: Nucleus
Mitochondrion
Chloroplast
Ribosome

questions.explanation: Chloroplasts contain chlorophyll and are the site of photosynthesis.

questions.text: Which insect transmits the malaria parasite to people?

options.text: The tsetse fly
The female Anopheles mosquito
The female Aedes mosquito
The male Anopheles mosquito

questions.explanation: Only female Anopheles mosquitoes feed on blood and carry Plasmodium. Aedes carries dengue and tsetse flies carry sleeping sickness.

questions.text: Two pea plants that are both heterozygous for height (Tt) are crossed, and T is dominant. What is the expected ratio of tall to short offspring?

options.text: 3 tall : 1 short
1 tall : 1 short
1 tall : 3 short
All tall

questions.explanation: Tt × Tt gives TT, Tt, Tt and tt, so three offspring show the dominant trait for every one with the recessive trait.

questions.text: During a practical, a pupil gets a few drops of dilute acid on her hand. What should you do first?

options.text: Rub the area with a dry cloth and let her continue the practical so she does not miss it
Do nothing at all if the pupil says there is no pain and the skin looks normal
Pour a strong alkali on the skin to neutralise the acid and stop it from burning
Rinse the area under plenty of running water, then check for irritation and report it

questions.explanation: Flushing with plenty of water dilutes and removes the acid. Neutralising with a strong alkali would cause further injury.

questions.text: Your school has no laboratory or equipment. How should you teach a lesson on states of matter?

options.text: Demonstrate with local materials such as water, ice and bottles and let pupils record observations
Skip practical work and let pupils copy the notes about solids, liquids and gases from the board into exercise books
Use only a textbook diagram of the three states and ask pupils not to interrupt the lesson with questions
Ask each pupil to buy laboratory apparatus from a shop and bring it to the next lesson

questions.explanation: Simple local materials allow observation and discussion, which help pupils understand better than copying notes.

questions.text: Pupils plan an experiment to find out whether fertiliser affects bean growth. Which design features make it a fair test? Select all that apply.

options.text: Keep soil, water, light and seed type the same for all plants
Use several plants for each condition and take the average growth
Use one plant for each condition and compare them
Give some plants more water to save time
Change only one variable, the amount of fertiliser

questions.explanation: A fair test changes one variable and controls others. Repeating with several plants reduces the effect of chance.

description: Checks computer-studies knowledge, safe internet practice and the ability to teach ICT with limited equipment.

competencies.name: Hardware and Software Fundamentals
competencies.description: Devices, memory, storage and types of software.

competencies.name: Office Productivity Tools
competencies.description: Word processing and spreadsheet skills including formulas.

competencies.name: Internet Safety and Digital Citizenship
competencies.description: Passwords, phishing, scams and protecting pupils online.

competencies.name: Programming and Computational Thinking
competencies.description: Reading simple code and understanding algorithms.

competencies.name: Teaching ICT with Limited Equipment
competencies.description: Organising lessons and assessment when computers are few.

questions.text: Which of these is an output device?

options.text: Mouse
Microphone
Printer
Scanner

questions.explanation: A printer produces output from the computer; the others send data into the computer.

questions.text: Which statement about RAM is correct?

options.text: It is the main processor that carries out calculations for the whole computer
It permanently stores all of the user's files even when there is no power
It is storage that is only used for photos, videos and other large media files
It is temporary working memory whose contents are lost when the power is off

questions.explanation: RAM is volatile memory used for programs and data in use; files are saved on storage such as a hard disk or SSD.

questions.text: Which of these is an example of an operating system?

options.text: Google Chrome
Microsoft Excel
PowerPoint
Windows

questions.explanation: An operating system manages the computer hardware and runs other programs. Excel, Chrome and PowerPoint are application software.

questions.text: Which spreadsheet formula gives the average of the values in cells B2 to B6?

options.text: =MEAN(B2:B6)
=AVERAGE(B2:B6)
=AVERAGE(B2:B6)/5
=SUM(B2:B6)

questions.explanation: AVERAGE(range) adds the values and divides by how many there are. MEAN is not a spreadsheet function.

questions.text: In a fee sheet, cell D2 contains =B2*C1 where C1 holds the discount rate. When copied down to D3, the result is wrong. What is the best fix?

options.text: Change D2 to =B2*$C$1 and copy it down again
Delete column C and enter the rate in each cell
Type each formula by hand in every row with the new C number
Change D2 to =B2*C2 and copy it down

questions.explanation: The $ signs make the reference to C1 absolute, so it does not move when the formula is copied.

questions.text: A pupil tells you a stranger on social media is asking for her photos and her home address. What is the best advice?

options.text: Ask the stranger to send his own photo and address first to prove who he is
Do not reply or share anything, block and report the person, and tell a trusted adult
Delete the messages straight away and tell nobody at home or at school
Reply politely and share only the home address but not the photos

questions.explanation: Pupils should never share personal information with strangers, and the incident should be reported to a trusted adult so they are protected.

questions.text: Which are features of a strong password? Select all that apply.

options.text: It is the same on every account so you can remember it
It mixes letters, numbers and symbols
It is long, for example 12 or more characters
It is different for each important account
It is your name followed by your birth year

questions.explanation: Long, varied and unique passwords are harder to guess and one stolen password does not open other accounts.

questions.text: A caller says he is from your mobile money provider and asks for your PIN to "reverse a wrong transfer". What should you do?

options.text: Share only the first two digits of the PIN so the caller can verify the account
Give the PIN quickly so that the wrong transfer can be reversed and the money returned
Send a small amount of money to the caller first to prove that the request is genuine
End the call, never share the PIN and contact the provider on its official number

questions.explanation: Providers never ask for your PIN. This is a common scam, so you should end the call and report it through official channels.

questions.text: What is the output of this Python code?  for i in range(3):  print(i)

options.text: 0 1 2 3 (each on a new line)
0 1 2 (each on a new line)
1 2 3 (each on a new line)

questions.explanation: range(3) produces 0, 1 and 2, so three numbers are printed starting from 0.

questions.text: What does this program print?  x = 5;  x = x + 2;  if x > 6: x = x - 3;  print(x * 2)
questions.explanation: x becomes 7, which is greater than 6, so x becomes 4. Then 4 × 2 = 8 is printed.

questions.text: You have 40 pupils and only 5 working computers. What is the best way to organise a practical lesson?

options.text: Let the pupils decide among themselves who may use a computer and who must wait
Let only the best pupils use the computers while the rest watch from their desks
Rotate small groups with defined roles on the computers while others do paper-based planning
Teach only theory from the notes and skip all practice because computers are few

questions.explanation: Rotation gives everyone hands-on time, and paper tasks keep the other pupils learning.

questions.text: Your school has a power cut and no computers for a week. Which activities can still teach ICT concepts? Select all that apply.

options.text: Ask pupils to memorise definitions only without any activity
Pupils draw a paper keyboard and practise finger positions
Pupils role-play input, processing, storage and output as a human computer
Cancel ICT lessons until new computers are bought
Pupils write step-by-step instructions or a flowchart for a daily task

questions.explanation: Unplugged activities teach hardware, typing and algorithm concepts without electricity.

description: Checks geography, history and civics knowledge for Tanzania and East Africa, map and source skills, and teaching approaches for social studies.

competencies.name: Geography
competencies.description: Physical and human geography of Tanzania and East Africa, including climate.

competencies.name: History
competencies.description: Key events in Tanzanian and East African history.

competencies.name: Civics and Citizenship
competencies.description: Government, rights and responsibilities of citizens.

competencies.name: Map Skills and Source Analysis
competencies.description: Reading maps and judging historical sources.

competencies.name: Teaching Methods and Assessment
competencies.description: Active methods for social studies and handling sensitive topics.

questions.text: Which is the largest lake in Africa by surface area?

options.text: Lake Rukwa
Lake Nyasa
Lake Tanganyika
Lake Victoria

questions.explanation: Lake Victoria is the largest African lake by area; Lake Tanganyika is the deepest.

questions.text: Why does the windward side of Mount Kilimanjaro receive heavy rainfall?

options.text: Air sinks and warms as it passes over the peak
Moist air is forced upwards, cools and condenses to form rain
Hot ground heats the air and causes daily thunderstorms
Strong tides carry sea water onto the slopes

questions.explanation: This is relief (orographic) rainfall: moist air rising over high ground cools, condenses and falls as rain.

questions.text: Which event took place on 26 April 1964?

options.text: The Union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar
Tanganyika's independence from Britain
The Zanzibar Revolution against the Sultan
The Arusha Declaration on socialism

questions.explanation: Union Day marks the union of Tanganyika and Zanzibar to form the United Republic. The Zanzibar Revolution was in January 1964.

questions.text: A pupil writes that "Africans accepted colonial taxes happily" based only on a colonial officer's report. How should you guide the pupil?

options.text: Tell the pupil that old documents cannot be used in history
Tell the pupil to remove all sources and just write from memory
Tell the pupil that official reports are always true because they were written at the time
Ask who wrote it and why, and compare it with other sources such as African oral accounts

questions.explanation: Sources have authors with viewpoints and purposes. Comparing different sources gives a more balanced conclusion.

questions.text: Which body makes laws in Mainland Tanzania?

options.text: The Police Force
The Judiciary
The President acting alone
The Parliament (Bunge)

questions.explanation: The Bunge is the legislature that passes laws. The judiciary interprets them and the executive implements them.

questions.text: During a class prefect election, some pupils complain that one candidate is giving out sweets for votes. How should you use this?

options.text: Punish the pupils who complained for creating trouble during the election
Discuss why bribery is unfair and let the class set rules for a fair election
Ignore the complaint because it is only a school election and not a national one
Cancel the election and appoint the prefect yourself without asking the class

questions.explanation: Practising fair rules teaches civic values such as honesty, equal opportunity and respect for the vote.

questions.text: Which are responsibilities of a good citizen? Select all that apply.

options.text: Choosing which laws to follow
Punishing suspected thieves yourself
Protecting public property such as school buildings and roads
Obeying the laws of the country
Paying taxes honestly as required by law

questions.explanation: Citizens have duties to support the state and the community; justice should be left to the courts and not to the public.

questions.text: On a map with scale 1:50,000, two villages are 4 cm apart. What is the real distance?

options.text: 20 km
4 km
2 km

questions.text: What was a main cause of the Maji Maji uprising (1905–1907) against German rule?

options.text: A dispute over borders set at the Berlin Conference
Forced cotton growing and harsh labour demands
Competition over clove plantations in Zanzibar
A British ban on the ivory trade

questions.explanation: Forced communal cotton cultivation and heavy labour demands angered many communities in southern Tanganyika.

questions.text: What mainly causes the two rainy seasons (masika and vuli) in northern and eastern Tanzania?

options.text: The tides of the Indian Ocean rising and falling twice in a year
Volcanic activity in the Rift Valley that releases moisture into the air
The north–south movement of the Inter-Tropical Convergence Zone (ITCZ)
Seasonal changes in the speed of the Earth's rotation on its axis

questions.explanation: The ITCZ passes over these areas twice a year as it moves north and south, bringing the two rainy seasons.

questions.text: Your pupils say history is boring because it is only dates to memorise. What is the best way to respond?

options.text: Dictate longer notes on every event and test the exact dates each week in class
Teach only the most recent history because it is easier for pupils to remember
Give lessons in complete silence so pupils concentrate on memorising names and dates
Use timelines, storytelling and role-play to link events to people's lives

questions.explanation: Active, story-based methods help pupils understand why events matter and remember them better than memorising dates.

questions.text: A class discussion about the Union becomes heated and pupils begin to insult each other. What should you do?

options.text: Declare which side is right and punish everyone on the other side in front of the class
Pause, remind pupils of the ground rules, and ask them to support their views with evidence
Stop all discussion of sensitive topics such as the Union for the rest of the year
Let the argument continue so that pupils learn to defend themselves without help

questions.explanation: Ground rules and evidence-based discussion allow pupils to explore sensitive topics respectfully.
